docs.title: About this portfolio...
docs.text:
Hi, I'm Emile.

I'm a technical writer who creates clear, structured documentation for complex topics. Outside of my day-to-day work, I upskill through independent projects that let me explore different documentation formats, authoring tools, and problem spaces.

This portfolio includes non-proprietary projects created outside of professional employment. Because of confidentiality and NDA restrictions, I don’t publish internal or client documentation. Most of these projects aim to showcase how I approach documentation and writing across formats such as online help systems, long-form PDFs, structured markup, and interactive prototypes.

Projects are grouped by documentation type. Each one includes context around scope, assumptions, and design decisions.

docs.title: Testing APIs with Postman
docs.text:
This project demonstrates hands-on API testing using Postman. It focuses on manually calling API endpoints, inspecting request and response data, and writing basic JavaScript tests to validate expected behavior. The intent is to show practical familiarity with API interactions and how testing supports developers, QA analysts, and documentation accuracy.

The project uses Spotify's API and prioritizes conceptual understanding over exhaustive test coverage.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Understanding of how APIs are called, requests constructed, and responses validated during testing
  • Writing lightweight JavaScript assertions to verify expected outcomes
  • Comfort working across documentation, development, and QA-adjacent workflows

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The intended audience is technical, with basic familiarity with APIs and HTTP concepts.
  • Testing focuses on validating expected behavior rather than uncovering edge cases or performance issues.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Automated testing workflows (such as Newman or Postman CLI) are intentionally out of scope.

docs.text:

docs.title: Documenting an open API specification project
docs.text:
This project is an OpenAPI specification for a fictional car rental service, created using Swagger Editor. The documentation describes endpoints for browsing inventory, making and deleting reservations, and other common API operations. Components, links, and polymorphic definitions are used where appropriate to adhere to OpenAPI best practices.

Some less critical endpoints are not fully fleshed out, as the focus of this project is on demonstrating proper API documentation structure and design rather than actual implementation.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Structuring an OpenAPI specification with clarity, reusability, and maintainability in mind
  • Documenting core functionality even when the API is partially defined

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The API is fictional; endpoint behavior is assumed for documentation purposes.
  • The primary audience is developers familiar with standard REST conventions.
  • The specification focuses on core operations (inventory browsing, reservations); less critical endpoints are intentionally omitted.
  • Security and error handling are documented for demonstration purposes only.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Edge-case endpoints and full implementation examples are intentionally out of scope, as the focus is on showcasing clear, maintainable, and standards-compliant API documentation.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
Try out the OpenAPI specification in Swagger UI:

Five Stars Rental Inventory API

docs.title: Retrieving data using SQL
docs.text:
This project uses SQL to analyze longevity data for various zoo animals. The queries are intermediate in complexity and are intended to demonstrate SQL familiarity in support of analysis and documentation-related work.

The results are presented as an HTML document generated with Asciidoctor, with light CSS customization to improve readability and structure.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to write intermediate SQL queries
  • Translating SQL queries output into clear, structured explanations
  • Presenting technical analysis in a polished, reader-friendly format
  • Comfort working with structured data

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The dataset is assumed to be clean for the purpose of analysis.
  • The audience is technical and familiar with basic database concepts.
  • The focus is on query logic and result interpretation rather than database administration.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Database design, indexing strategies, and optimization are intentionally out of scope.

docs.title: Writing a book chapter on American military culture and identities
docs.text:
I co-authored a book chapter called Schoolhouses and COCOMs: Educating and Cultivating the American-Led International Fraternity of the Uniform, appearing in Culture and the Soldier: Identities, Values, and Norms in Military Engagements, published by UBC Press.

My chapter analyzes how professional military education institutions and combatant commands (COCOMs) reinforce norms and identities within the American-led military order. It explores this transmission of culture elevates interoperability among allied forces beyond formal doctrine.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to contribute original analysis to a peer-reviewed, multi-author volume
  • Comfort working within conceptual frameworks and editorial constraints
  • Ability translating abstract concepts into concrete terms

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The reader has baseline familiarity with military institutions or security studies.
  • Culture is treated as an analytical tool rather than a normative argument.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This chapter examines how professional military education and command structures have helped shape military norms and identities in the 21st century. Policy prescriptions are outside the scope of the contribution.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
Link to the book:

Culture and the Soldier: Identities, Values, and Norms in Military Engagements

docs.title: Writing a peer-reviewed paper on American foreign policy
docs.text:
This article examines the tension between U.S. grand strategy and public support, using the 2016 presidential transition as a focal point. It analyzes whether a turn toward isolationism and nationalism meaningfully alters America’s long-standing strategic behavior, given its tradition of global engagement and liberal interventionism.

Rather than treating grand strategy as elite-driven alone, the paper highlights public opinion as a constraining factor, discussing likely strategic outcomes when the public is unwilling to bear the costs of hegemonic leadership.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to analyze complex political and strategic concepts with nuance
  • Academic research, synthesis, and formal argumentative writing

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The reader has baseline familiarity with international relations or political science concepts.
  • The article is evaluated for analytical rigor rather than policy prescription.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This paper analyzes U.S. grand strategy and public attitudes during a specific political moment.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
Access the peer-reviewed article on JSTOR:

The Public Costs of Grand Strategy in the Trump Era

docs.title: Writing a peer-reviewed paper on U.S. politics
docs.text:
This essay was written in 2015 in partial fulfillment of my Master’s degree and was subsequently published in the Journal of Military and Strategic Studies, where it received the award for best essay in the volume.

The paper analyzes the U.S. “pivot” toward the Asia-Pacific and evaluates its effectiveness as a hedging strategy in managing China’s rising power. It argues that the pivot remains (at that time) a viable and stabilizing strategy as U.S. and Chinese interests in the region do (did) not fundamentally conflict.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to synthesize dense theoretical and empirical literature
  • Clear, structured argumentation over long-form analytical writing

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The reader has baseline familiarity with international relations theory and security studies.
  • Strategic behavior is analyzed within historical context.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This article focuses on U.S.–China relations in the Asia-Pacific during the Obama administration. Post-2015 developments are out of scope.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
The peer-reviewed paper is available for download:

docs.title: Writing a byline on rare diseases
docs.text:
To keep my copywriting skills current, I occasionally take on small freelance engagements when time allows. In this instance, I wrote a press release for a U.S.-based non-profit organization aimed at raising awareness of rare diseases. The article was subsequently picked up by a media outlet.

This sample demonstrates my ability to work with academic and scientific sources, interpret research findings, extract relevant data, and translate complex information into clear, accessible, and persuasive copy for a general audience.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to research and synthesize academic and scientific literature
  • Judgment in selecting relevant statistics and framing them for a non-technical audience
  • Experience writing persuasive copy suitable for public-facing media

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Readers have limited prior knowledge of rare diseases or related policy issues.
  • The primary goal is awareness and clarity rather than technical depth.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This project focuses on a single press-style article.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
Read the article online:

Rare Disease Day 2024: IndoUSrare's Frontline Efforts in Tackling Global Inequities

docs.title: Writing a thought leadership article on solar energy
docs.text:
CPCS, a global infrastructure consulting firm, developed a strategy to address Mozambique’s energy constraints through solar power combined with battery storage. I was engaged to ghostwrite a thought leadership article explaining this approach and the associated energy procurement strategy. The article was later published by Energy Global, a leading magazine in electrical engineering, and received wide readership.

This sample highlights my ability to work closely with subject-matter experts, ask effective questions, and transform technical concepts into an engaging and accessible narrative suitable for the general public.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to obtain and synthesize expert knowledge through interviews
  • Editorial judgment in balancing technical accuracy with readability
  • Narrative framing for thought leadership and industry publications

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The target audience includes industry professionals and informed non-specialists
  • Readers may have limited familiarity with Mozambique’s energy infrastructure

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The article is intended to position expertise rather than provide implementation guidance. Engineering specifications, financial modeling, and policy analysis are out of scope.

docs.title: Writing a tabletop role-playing game content with Homebrewery
docs.text:
This project is a piece of original lore describing a wuxia-inspired guild of wandering warriors created for a Dungeons & Dragons setting. While primarily a creative writing exercise, it is also designed to closely follow established D&D publishing conventions in terms of structure, layout, and visual presentation.

The document was formatted using Homebrewery, a web-based tool that enables creators to produce D&D content using a Markdown-like syntax.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to write clear, engaging narrative and explanatory content within a rigid stylistic framework
  • Attention to formatting, hierarchy, and visual consistency
  • Ability to make custom content look indistinguishable from professionally published material

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The reader has basic familiarity with Dungeons & Dragons or tabletop role-playing games.
  • The material is intended for experimental play, not competitive balance.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This project includes narrative lore, character concepts, stat blocks, and custom mechanical elements. Playtesting, balance considerations, and campaign integration are intentionally out of scope.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:

docs.title: Writing a tabletop role-playing game content with LaTex
docs.text:
This project is a compendium of homebrewed Dungeons & Dragons weapons, armor, and other wondrous items inspired by the equipment of selected League of Legends characters. Each entry includes both flavor text and clearly defined 5e-based gameplay mechanics.

The document was authored and typeset entirely in LaTeX, allowing precise control over layout, presentation, and consistency across entries.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to document rules-based content with clear structure and repeatable patterns
  • Proficiency with LaTeX for producing polished, print-ready documents

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The content is evaluated as a documentation and presentation exercise.
  • The reader has basic familiarity with Dungeons & Dragons 5e rules.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This project focuses on item descriptions, flavor text, and mechanical definitions. Playtesting, balance considerations, and campaign integration are intentionally out of scope.

docs.title: Writing a data integration guide for Prophix
docs.text:
This project is a conceptual data integration guide created as part of an interview assessment for Prophix Software Ltd. The guide focuses on describing the main steps of an ERP integration at a high level, with brief references to core concepts provided through a glossary.

The guide demonstrates the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar technical domains, organize information logically, and communicate complex processes clearly with limited source material. The document was written and typeset from scratch using LaTeX.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Translating engineer input into a structured, reader-friendly process narrative
  • Judging when high-level explanation is more appropriate than deep technical references
  • Producing polished, long-form documentation using LaTeX

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The intended reader is a client with general technical familiarity who is not directly involved in ERP implementation.
  • The guide assumes that implementation tasks will be delegated IT resources after the material is reviewed.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The guide focus on explaining what happens at each stage rather than how to configure systems. Troubleshooting and edge cases are out of scope.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
The data integration guide in PDF is available for download:

Download the data integration guide

docs.title: Building and parsing XML with Eclipse IDE
docs.text:
In this project, I build an XML schema for a vehicle maintenance log in Eclipse IDE and use Java to create three parsers (DOM, SAX, and STAX) to process the resulting XML file. The schema defines the structure and rules used to ensure the XML data is formatted and validated consistently.

The aim of this project is to demonstrate my ability to write XML documents and schemas, as well as my ability to research and implement the appropriate Java code needed to parse structured XML content.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Understanding of how XML data is validated and consumed
  • Familiarity with XML parsing approaches (DOM, SAX, STAX)
  • Resourcefulness in researching and applying unfamiliar code

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The schema is intended for internal or instructional use.
  • The XML files being parsed are valid.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The Java parsers are illustrative rather than fully optimized. Error handling and real-world integration are out of scope.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
The XML schema and parsers are available for download:

Download the .zip folder

docs.title: Generating online documentation with MkDocs
docs.text: This project is an online help system for a fictional car recognition app, built using MkDocs. The content is written in Markdown and organized through a custom mkdocs.yml configuration to show how I think about structure, navigation, and topic organization. I also added light CSS customization to improve readability and overall presentation.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Designing navigation and topic hierarchy in MkDocs
  • Writing task-oriented help content for a non-technical audience
  • Applying light visual customization

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The app is a consumer-facing mobile application with a relatively simple feature set.
  • The primary audience is a first-time or casual user with no prior familiarity with the app.
  • Product behavior and feature details are fabricated for the purpose of documentation, as the app is fictional.
  • The help content prioritizes clarity over exhaustive feature coverage.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This help system covers onboarding and core app functionality. It is not intended to be a production-ready help center.

Troubleshooting, edge cases, and accessibility considerations are intentionally out of scope.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
The online help system is available on GitHub:

CarSnap Documentation

docs.title: Writing a webhelp on the mutant apocalypse
docs.text: This project is a short WebHelp guide on surviving a hypothetical mutant apocalypse, created using Oxygen XML and DITA. The content is authored as individual DITA topics and organized through a DITA map, with light CSS customization applied to the output. The project aims to demonstrate structured, topic-based authoring in DITA and familiarity with the Oxygen authoring environment.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Structuring content into discrete, reusable DITA topics
  • Organizing topics and relationships through a DITA map
  • Applying CSS to customize the layout and presentation of WebHelp output

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The content covers a fictional mutant apocalypse scenario; details are invented for demonstration purposes.
  • The audience is a survivor seeking explanatory information, not performing tasks.
  • The WebHelp system is viewed in a modern browser; no device constraints are assumed.
  • The project focuses on clarity and structure rather than usability testing.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The project includes explanatory topics that outline the scenario and survival concepts. Only a subset of potential topics is included; advanced scenarios are intentionally excluded.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
The online help system is available on GitHub:

How to Survive the Mutant Apocalypse

docs.title: Writing a webhelp for Nectari
docs.text:
This project is a conceptual online help system for Nectari Software Inc.'s "Formula Wizard" feature, created as part of an interview assessment using ClickHelp (trial version). The project involved organizing content, writing explanatory topics, and demonstrating how a help system could structure and present the feature to end users. A French version of the help system was also created, demonstrating consideration for multilingual support.

The original hosted output is no longer available; this portfolio shows a write-up of the mock-up to highlight the approach, structure, and writing style. An offer was extended, but I chose not to accept it.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Designing an online help system conceptually, including content hierarchy, visual support, and navigation
  • Writing explanatory topics that clarify feature functionality for end users
  • Understanding and writing about advanced accounting concepts under time constraint
  • Considering localization and multilingual support (English/French toggle)

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The intended audience is an accountant new to the "Formula Wizard" feature
  • The project is a conceptual mock-up; live testing was not possible.
  • The focus is on content clarity and organization rather than interactivity with the product.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The project demonstrates planning, writing, and structuring documentation for evaluation purposes only. Visual design and advanced ClickHelp functionality are intentionally excluded.

docs.title: Check It Out
docs.text:
A write-up of the Nectari Formula Wizard mock-up is available for download:

Download the Nectari Help System write-up

docs.title: Writing a video game guide using Adobe XD
docs.text:
This project is an incomplete gameplay guide for playing Jarvan IV as an ADC in League of Legends, created in Adobe XD. While the topic is niche, the goal is to showcase my ability to effectively design and present instructional content.

The emphasis is on layout and presentation rather than on the game itself. Readers unfamiliar with League of Legends should still be able to follow the structure and evaluate the design choices.

docs.title: What this project demonstrates
docs.text:
• Ability to design instructional content using a UX and prototyping tool
  • Separation of concepts, logic, and contextual explanations
  • Attention to layout, presentation, and readability

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• The reader is familiar with League of Legends; understanding of gameplay concepts are assumed.
  • The guide is evaluated primarily as a presentation and design exercise.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Explanation of core gameplay concepts and mechanics are intentionally left out of scope.
